record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Let X be a smooth contractible complex affine algebraic surface of log-general type. Does X contain any once-punctured curve? If so, are there only finitely many such curves?

evidence.quote:
QUESTION. Does X contain any once-punctured curve ? Does it contain only a
finite number of such curves ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth contractible complex affine algebraic surface that is of log-general type (i.e., for any smooth projective completion $\bar X$ of $X$ with simple normal crossing boundary divisor $D=\bar X\setminus X$, the log Kodaira dimension $\bar\kappa(X)=\kappa(\bar X, K_{\bar X}+D)$ equals $2$). By a once-punctured curve on $X$ we mean a closed algebraic curve $C\subset X$ such that the normalization of $C$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{A}^1\setminus\{0\}=\mathbb{C}^*$ (equivalently, $C$ is irreducible with exactly one place at infinity in $X$ and geometric genus $0$ with one puncture from its smooth completion).

(a) Does such an $X$ necessarily contain a once-punctured curve?

(b) If $X$ does contain once-punctured curves, must the set of such curves be finite?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a definitive resolution of these questions about once-punctured curves on smooth contractible affine surfaces of log-general type. The general topic (contractible affine surfaces, curves with few places at infinity) is actively studied, but no source clearly settles existence/finiteness in this generality.
